extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and authors preparing/submitting expository articles or book reviews to the Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and policies for authors preparing and submitting expository research articles, book reviews (by invitation), and short Mathematical Perspectives pieces to the Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and types of content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin publishes expository articles on contemporary mathematical research, written in a way that gives insight to mathematicians who may not be experts in the particular topic. The Bulletin also publishes reviews of selected books in mathematics and short articles in the Mathematical Perspectives section, both by invitation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be expository in nature, aimed at a mathematically literate but not necessarily specialist audience. Book reviews and Mathematical Perspectives pieces are only by invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (Centralized Manuscript Processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS uses Centralized Manuscript Processing for initial submissions to AMS journals. The preferred method of submission is to upload a PDF file using the Initial Manuscript Submission form. An alternate method is to send one copy of the paper to Centralized Manuscript Processing, Bulletin of the AMS, 201 Charles Street, Providence, Rhode Island 02904-2213 USA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the alternate paper submission, required information must accompany the submission (see 'Required submission information'). Authors should consult the Initial Manuscript Submission form for online submission and prefer PDF upload. The author should suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper that has been previously published, or is being considered for publication elsewhere, should be submitted to the American Mathematical Society, nor may a paper that is under consideration by the American Mathematical Society be submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition on duplicate publication and simultaneous submissions. Ensure the manuscript is not published or under review elsewhere before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission information and contact details
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper copy is being forwarded to the AMS, the following information is required with the submission (note that all contact information, particularly email addresses, must be supplied to avoid delay): Name of the journal to which the paper is submitted; Name of the corresponding author; Contact information including email address and mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete and accurate contact details for the corresponding author and suggest an appropriate Editor. Missing or incorrect contact information may delay processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (2020 MSC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Included with the footnotes to the paper should be the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification representing the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List primary and secondary MSC codes in the footnotes as part of the submission metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract is required. It should be a brief technical description of the new material. The AMS offers free worldwide access to the electronic abstracts. No abstracts appear in the printed journal starting in 1998.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a concise, technical abstract suitable for free online indexing and discovery. Abstracts, references (with links to MathSciNet), and bibliographic information are freely viewable for every article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance obligations (Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a paper has been accepted for publication, authors should follow the online Submission Instructions. All authors must submit the Consent to Publish. All authors must agree regarding the Copyright Agreement. If the article is to be published in one of the AMS Open Access journals, authors must agree which Creative Commons License will be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required post-acceptance paperwork (Consent to Publish, Copyright Agreement). For Open Access publications, authors must decide on the Creative Commons license to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AMS style files and preparation resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS Author Resource Center provides TeX Resources, the AMS Style Guide, the Mathematics Subject Classification, and further useful tools for preparing your manuscript. Authors are encouraged to use AMS-prepared style files in preparing their papers. Useful tools include AMS journal article templates from Overleaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AMS style files and templates to format submissions. Consult the Author Resource Center for TeX resources and the AMS Style Guide to reduce formatting issues and speed processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and graphics preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint Author Guidelines for Preparing Accessible Mathematics Content and guidance on preparing graphics are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the joint author guidelines to prepare accessible mathematics content and properly formatted graphics; consult provided resources for best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions, copying, and republication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual readers of this publication, and nonprofit libraries acting for them, are permitted to make fair use of the material, such as to copy an article for use in teaching or research. Permission is granted to quote brief passages from this publication in reviews, provided the customary acknowledgment of the source is given. Republication, systematic copying, or multiple reproduction of any material in this publication is permitted only under license from the American Mathematical Society. Requests for permission to reuse portions of AMS publication content are handled by the Copyright Clearance Center. Excluded from these provisions is material for which the author holds copyright. In such cases, requests for permission to reuse or reprint material should be addressed directly to the author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For republication or systematic reuse obtain a license via the Copyright Clearance Center. If the author retains copyright for particular material, contact the author directly for reuse permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication cycle and early view policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society is published quarterly with articles electronically published individually to the AMS website before appearing in an issue. Articles are published on the AMS website individually soon after proof is returned from authors and before appearing in an issue (most recently published article listed first). Early View PDF articles are an AMS member benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware articles may appear online individually prior to issue assignment; consult AMS policy on making changes to articles after publication and on citing articles before they appear in an issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints and author access
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints are provided free of charge in electronic form to all authors. A downloadable and printable PDF version of each article is available from the AMS website following print publication. Notification email containing access information is sent to all authors as soon as an issue is published in print. This electronic delivery system provides authors with permanent electronic access to their published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors receive electronic offprints and permanent access via emailed access information after print publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and archiving information
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal is indexed in Mathematical Reviews®, Science Citation Index®, Science Citation Index—Expanded, ISI Alerting Services, CompuMath Citation Index®, and Current Content®/Physical, Chemical & Earth Sciences. This journal is archived in Portico and in CLOCKSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may reference this indexing and archiving when considering visibility and long-term preservation of published work.
